chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a launderer to whom goods are handed over, and he burns them or tears them. Is he held liable for compensation?
He عليه السلام said: "Yes, make him liable for what his hand has caused, for you only gave it to him so that he might repair it, and you did not give it to him so that he might ruin it."

key_terms.الْقَصَّارِ: the launderer or cloth-cleaner entrusted with the item
key_terms.الْمَتَاعُ: the goods or property handed over to the worker
key_terms.جَنَتْ يَدُهُ: what his own hand committed or caused
key_terms.لِيُصْلِحَ: so that he may fix or improve it
key_terms.يُغَرَّمُهُ: he is made liable for compensation

ai.seo_question: Is a launderer or repair worker liable if he damages the item entrusted to him?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a worker entrusted with another person's property is liable when he damages it through his own act. The Imam عليه السلام grounds the ruling in the purpose of the entrustment: the item was given for benefit and repair, not for harm and فساد. It is significant in fiqh for establishing liability in cases of negligent or damaging conduct by hired craftsmen.
